answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Think of a wharf that charges every arriving ship a refundable bond: agents post a small stake before they can transact, and misbehavior forfeits it, so spawning ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand stakes. Trust then grows slowly, like an ember catching hold — newcomers start with narrow limits and earn wider access only through attested, useful work. One marble of reputation proves nothing; a sustained history of costly, verified actions does.
